intent: Implement offline workload injection and reviewable preview

name: ManifestStream
role: Parses and renders complete Kubernetes YAML streams in the CLI
conditions: Rejects duplicate keys, non-object documents and unsafe YAML tags before transformation

title: chose structured YAML parsing over text substitution
why: Kubernetes resources contain nested structures and multiple documents that must be validated before the Helm post-renderer emits output
alternative: Text substitution — rejected: can change the wrong nested field or emit incomplete output

name: WorkloadDiscovery
role: Selects an opted-in Deployment container and validates its explicit Java launch
conditions: Missing image entrypoints and ambiguous container selection require explicit configuration

title: chose explicit launch validation over guessing image entrypoints
why: A Helm manifest does not contain image-provided entrypoint defaults, so guessing could replace the real application command
alternative: Infer the launch from incomplete manifests — rejected: original arguments may not be available

intent: Generate reversible workload and trainer resources

name: OfflineInjector
role: Transforms opted-in Deployments and generates trainer resources offline
conditions: Stores original launch for reinjection and removal; requires conflict and runtime validation before release

title: chose a versioned ownership marker for reversible injection
why: The original command and args can be absent or contain boundaries that cannot be reconstructed from a wrapper
alternative: Infer original command from wrapper arguments — rejected: cannot preserve absent fields and future transformations reliably

intent: Preserve workload mounts in generated resources

name: Generated trainer and fetch containers
role: Reuse workload image, environment and mounts for discovery and training
conditions: Volume and identity compatibility still require end-to-end verification

title: chose to preserve application mounts in trainer and fetch
why: Application JARs and configuration may reside in mounted volumes, not only the image
alternative: Copy image and environment alone — rejected: mounted workload inputs would be missing

name: inject CLI
role: Reads a Kubernetes stream and emits transformed YAML or preview diagnostics
conditions: Errors return nonzero before manifest output; preview diff remains follow-up

title: chose complete-stream validation before emitting Helm output
why: Helm consumes standard output as a resource stream and partial output could describe an incomplete transformation
alternative: Emit each resource during processing — rejected: a later failure would follow earlier output

intent: Add redacted preview and explicit namespace handling

name: ManifestDiff
role: Reports structural changes without disclosing field values
conditions: Preview identifies changed paths and generated resources

name: Namespace selection
role: Places generated trainer resources alongside the workload
conditions: An explicit namespace is required when rendered metadata omits it

title: chose an explicit namespace over assuming default
why: Helm-rendered resources may omit namespace even when the release targets a non-default namespace
alternative: Assume default — rejected: trainer resources could be created in a different namespace

intent: Protect managed fields and separate registry credentials

name: Managed field snapshots
role: Detects edits to injected workload fields before reinjection or removal
conditions: Conflicts fail the transformation instead of replacing user changes

name: Registry secret references
role: Supply separate pull and push credentials to fetch and training

title: chose managed-field comparison before restoration
why: Reconciliation must not silently erase edits made to previously injected fields
alternative: Always restore stored values — rejected: would overwrite user changes

intent: Detect edits to generated trainer resources

name: Generated resource checksum
role: Detects changes to generated trainer resources on later offline transformations
conditions: Checksum is a conflict detector, not a signature or authorization mechanism

title: chose checksummed generated resources over blind replacement
why: Reinjection should report edits to owned trainer resources rather than silently discard them
alternative: Replace generated resources unconditionally — rejected: user edits could be lost

intent: Validate injection resources and command overrides

name: Command override validation
role: Accepts a JSON string array for the original Java launch
conditions: Argument boundaries are retained and YAML shorthand is rejected

subject: Kubernetes resource schema validation
why: The generated Deployment and trainer resources were accepted by an isolated kind API server with server-side dry run; the live training path remains unverified

title: chose strict JSON arrays for launch overrides
why: A single unambiguous representation preserves argument boundaries across tools
alternative: Accept YAML shorthand — rejected: the annotation contract specifies JSON and parsers may interpret shorthand differently

intent: Verify on a real cluster, derive the tools image from the release, complete the preview

title: derive the injector's tools image from the CLI's release version and stamp that version into the tools image
why: The injector had the tools tag pinned to 0.2.0, which goes stale at the next release. The CLI ships inside that same image, so its own release version is the tag. A development build has no release version and must be told the image (--tools-image, also the way to use a private mirror) instead of silently pinning one. The image build did not stamp the version either (v0.2.0's image printed 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT), so it now runs versions:set from the VERSION build argument.
alternative: Keep a constant and bump it by hand at each release — rejected: it was already stale-prone and nothing would catch it

title: resolve the tools image lazily, only when a workload is opted in
why: A post-renderer runs over every chart; a stream with nothing opted in must pass through unchanged and must not fail because a development build cannot name an image. Codex's existing preview test caught the eager version.
alternative: Resolve at startup — rejected: breaks pass-through

title: list what the trainer copies from the workload in the preview, by name only
why: ADR 0007 requires the preview to list copied environment, Secret and volume references and the trainer identity. The trainer starts the application for real with that configuration, so a reviewer must see it; names (env names, Secret/ConfigMap names, volume names and kinds, mount paths) are shown, values never.
alternative: Hide everything as values hidden — rejected: not reviewable

title: reject Deployment names longer than 63 characters
why: The Deployment name is the owner label value on the generated resources and a label value is limited to 63 characters; the API server would reject the output after the render. Failing early with the length is clearer than truncating, which would break ownership detection.
alternative: Truncate or hash the label value — rejected: ownership is recomputed from the label

title: document that Helm 4 post-renderers are plugins instead of claiming the script form works
why: Helm's reference for 4.3.1 says --post-renderer takes the name of a post-renderer plugin; the script form is Helm 3's interface. It could not be tested on Helm 4 here (downloading the binary was blocked), so the doc states what is established, what is not tested, and a pipeline alternative.
alternative: Say it works with Helm — rejected: untested and contradicted by the reference

name: mnemo-warmup inject
role: Offline Helm post-renderer and preview: opted-in Deployments are wrapped and their trainer resources emitted in the same stream; reinjection is deterministic, disabling restores the original launch
conditions: Helm 3 interface for the script form; needs an explicit Java launch, a store URL and a trainer mode; the stream is rejected as a whole on any error

subject: Real cluster result
why: Through helm upgrade --install --post-renderer on kind: uncached start, trainer TRAINED, restarted pod uses the archive with java as PID 1, an unchanged upgrade leaves the manifest identical, disabling removes the generated resources and restores the command, re-enabling reuses the archive

subject: Helm 4
why: --post-renderer takes a plugin name in 4.x per Helm's reference; the executable-path form is Helm 3's; untested on Helm 4

subject: Pipeline environment prefix
why: VAR=value before the first command of a pipeline applies only to that command, not to later stages, so a shim on PATH must be exported for the whole pipeline
